summary: The translation is faithful and complete in its words, but it lost the full stop after עליך and the capital of 'The Merciful One', merged לדרוש ולחקור into one verb, rendered רז"ל as 'Sages', and misplaced the Machzor Vitry quotation marks (the author's introduction and the Mishnah were inside them). Several verses went unrecognised (Neh 2:2, Isa 29:15, Ps 36:3, Jon 1:6, Exod 35:35, Joel 2:20, 2 Sam 16:13) and מה לך נרדם was given the wrong sense. Five points are raised as questions: ראב"ע, כ' ע"ש and the quotation opening, בבחירתא, bat kol, קטיגורין.

patches.value: 9) And you, our friend, it was not enough for you that you did not do any one of all these but you believed their words and accepted their lies on the testimony of one witness and one judge and not in the presence of the litigant without inquiry, without investigation, without examination and you enjoyed their words and you also helped to strengthen their lies and it was fixed in your mind as the truth itself until you wrote that I am no longer able to deny it, etc. And you did not take to heart that testimony is accepted only in the presence of the litigant and that you are obliged to investigate and inquire into them with seven inquiries, investigations and examinations, as you are commanded. All the more so, since they did their deeds in the dark and smoothed their tongues to you in secret with their words to find a fault to hate and you were obliged to silence them with a rebuke. This is nothing but wickedness of heart: that you enjoy and long for their gossip and their informing. The Merciful One save us from this opinion! And it is possible that you too add of your own false informing, in order to honor yourself at the disgrace of your friends. And in the chapter Arvei Pesachim (115) we read: "Rav Sheshet said in the name of R. A.: whoever tells evil talk and whoever bears false witness against his fellow deserves to be thrown to the dogs, as it is said: 'to the dog you shall throw it' and it is written explicitly: 'you shall not carry a false report'; and it is read in it: 'you shall not cause to bear'". And we find several more homilies of our Rabbis of blessed memory on the punishment of one who tells evil talk. And in Machzor Vitry, tractate Avot, on what we learned, "do not judge your fellow until you reach his place", he writes, see there: "that the same transgression may come into your hand and you may be saved and escape from it, as we find with Jeroboam son of Nebat, that when Solomon married the daughter of Pharaoh, she brought in to him every kind of song in the world and said to him: 'So they do for such-and-such idolatry'. One time, he went to sleep, and the day grew late. She went and called the wood-carvers and the builders, who do the work of the craftsman and the designer, and they made over his bed the likeness of a firmament, and in it the sun, the moon, the stars and the constellations. In the morning he woke from his sleep to open the doors of the Temple, for the keys of the Temple were under his pillow. He saw that the firmament was bright with stars and the host, thinking that the night had not yet passed, he went back to sleep. And he slept four more hours, until he understood and recognised for himself that the night was not so long. And concerning that hour we learned a testimony about the morning daily offering, that was offered at four hours, in the Bechirta. Before he woke from his sleep, Jeroboam son of Nebat went to the door of his house, and a voice passed: 'Wicked one, how long will you sleep and neglect the morning daily offering? What is the matter with you, sleeper? Arise, call upon your God!' A bat kol came out and said to him: 'Wicked one, son of a wicked one, you are destined to abolish from Israel many, many offerings wilfully. And you hold him liable for the inadvertent as for the wilful. And for the coerced as for the voluntary!' And this is what is written: 'When Ephraim spoke there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel, but he incurred guilt through Baal and died'. This is said of Jeroboam, who was of the tribe of Ephraim, the trembling was the accuser against Solomon, he, Jeroboam, was prince in Israel and king, and the bat kol answered him that he would become guilty through Baal and die." Thus far his words. And you have done greatly and added to doing evil more than Jeroboam son of Nebat. For after you brought us to the prison by false informing before our exalted government! You called out all the people to go out to the cemetery, and commanded them to throw dust upon their heads for no reason. Not for a light commandment that we neglected, and not for a weighty commandment, God forbid, but because we walked according to the customs of our forefathers and set our learning in the Mishnah and in the Talmud and the Rambam and Shulchan Aruch to learn and to teach, to keep and to do. And we did not study further in a forged book, the book the Zohar, as is your custom.
patches.reason: Pausing and terminal punctuation lost (the full stop after עליך; the sentence start of רחמנא ליצלן); לדרוש ולחקור rendered by one verb; רוע לב; רז"ל is 'our Rabbis' by the ruling, not 'Sages'; Mahzor is Machzor by the scheme; the author's introduction and the Mishnah were inside the Machzor Vitry quotation marks, the Mishnah as a nested quotation (marks placed by sense: the opening formula כ' stands outside); מלאכת חרש וחושב; פנה לילה is 'passed'; ויעבר קול 'a voice passed'; מה לך נרדם (Jon 1:6) is 'what is the matter with you', not 'what is it to you'; רשע בן רשע; the coerced; לעפר בעפר is 'throw dust'; כמנהגי is plural; בספר מזויף is indefinite; הגדלת; run-on sentences without stops

patches.value: ידידנו: "our friend", the form of address, kept
patches.reason: The note called it ironic; the Hebrew does not say so
לדרוש is 'investigate' (cf. דרישה, 3:9.27); the English had one verb for the two verbs לדרוש ולחקור
לחקור is 'inquire' (cf. חקירה, 3:9.25)

patches.value: במחשך מעשיהם: echoes Isa 29:15 ("והיה במחשך מעשיהם", "their deeds are in the dark")
patches.reason: Embedded verse; list it

patches.value: והחליקו ... אליך ... למצוא עון לשנוא (3:9.74-81): echoes Ps 36:3 ("כי החליק אליו בעיניו למצא עונו לשנא"); "smoothed" is החליק, as in the verse
patches.reason: Embedded verse; list it

patches.value: רוע לב: "wickedness of heart", the printed word; the phrase echoes Neh 2:2 ("אין זה כי אם רע לב", "sadness of heart"); the likelier word of the verse is רע, but here the sense is wickedness
patches.reason: Embedded verse with a changed word; recorded as ruled
The author writes only קי"ה, with no דף; the English has "(115)" and the gloss and literal added "folio"

patches.value: קי"ה: the numeral 115, as the author gives it; he writes no "folio" and none is added
patches.reason: Follows the ruling: no reference is completed

patches.value: ראב"ע: four letters, ר-א-ב-ע; not expanded in the print. The usual acronym of Rabbi Eleazar ben Azariah, and also of Ibn Ezra (who cannot be meant in a Talmudic citation). Read as "R. A." by the ruling for an unexpanded name; the expansion is not stated in the text
patches.reason: Proposed ruling: keep "R. A." with this note, as for ר"א; the editor may decide to expand ראב"ע as "R. Eleazar ben Azariah" since the acronym has one usual Talmudic expansion
רז"ל is "our Rabbis of blessed memory" by the ruling; "Sages" is for חז"ל

patches.value: לרז"ל: רז"ל, "our Rabbis of blessed memory" (רבותינו זכרונם לברכה)
patches.reason: Fixed form
Scheme: ח = ch, as in Machzor, Pesachim, Shulchan Aruch

patches.value: מחזור ויטרי: Machzor Vitry, a compilation of prayers, laws and customs from the school of Rashi; it includes tractate Avot with a commentary
patches.reason: Book title: meaning at its first occurrence in the unit

patches.value: את: the sign of the definite object; it has no English word
patches.reason: Learner note
כ' is כתב (he writes); the expansion belongs in the gloss
ע"ש is "see there" or "on account of" by the ruling; "there" is neither

patches.value: ע"ש: by the ruling "see there" (עיין שם) or "on account of" (על שם). Read as "see there", the words in the author's voice, and the Machzor Vitry quotation opens at שתבא ("that the same transgression ..."); if על שם is meant the sense is "he writes: on account of the fact that the same transgression ...". The English is a plain "he writes, see there:" and the alternative is in `readings`
patches.reason: Proposed ruling: כ' ע"ש = "he writes, see there:", the marks opening after it (an opening formula stands outside the mark); the author's introduction and the Mishnah (על for אל) are his own words, not part of the quotation

patches.value: את: the sign of the definite object; it has no English word
patches.reason: Learner note
חרשי is "craftsmen of"; "of wood" is the next word
העץ is "the wood"
מלאכת
חרש in Exod 35:35, which the phrase echoes ("מלאכת חרש וחשב"); a noun, not "carving"
חושב (Exod 35:35 חשב), the skilled designer or weaver of patterns; a noun
פנה לילה, like פנה יום, is "the night had passed"; "had turned" does not say it
שקרב is a past form

patches.value: בבחירתא: an Aramaic word, from בחירה, "choice, chosen"; the author does not say what it names (it may be the Temple, "the Chosen House", or a place or text). Transliterated, not identified
patches.reason: Proposed ruling: keep the transliteration "the Bechirta" with this note; the alternative "in the Chosen House" is in `readings`. The pack names no source and none is added
ויעבר is "and passed"; "went out" is the verb of the bat kol (יצתה)

patches.value: ויעבר קול: echoes 1 Kgs 22:36 ("ויעבר הרנה במחנה", "a cry passed through the camp") and Ezra 1:1 ("ויעבר קול", the proclamation)
patches.reason: Embedded verse

patches.value: מה לך נרדם קום קרא אל אלהיך: Jon 1:6, the captain to Jonah asleep. "מה לך" is "what is the matter with you", not "what is it to you"
patches.reason: Verse unrecognised and the sense of מה לך wrong; the voice quotes Jon 1:6

patches.value: בת קול: literally "daughter of a voice", the heavenly voice of rabbinic tradition; kept as "bat kol" and explained in `context`
patches.reason: Proposed ruling: transliterate "bat kol" (the conventional English term, as the translator did), with the literal sense in this note at the first occurrence
רשע is a vocative, as at 3:9.288
"son of a wicked one"; "man" is not in the Hebrew

patches.value: מחייבו: participle with the suffix "him": "you hold him liable"; "him" is Solomon, as the end of the passage shows
patches.reason: The note spoke of pointing, but the Hebrew is unpointed
"the forced one" adds a word
רתת is the noun of Hos 13:1, "trembling", as at 3:9.331, not a verb

patches.value: רתת: "trembling", the word of the verse (Hos 13:1), which the author glosses as קטיגורין
patches.reason: The note called it a name of the accuser
קטיגורין is a Greek loanword, "accuser"

patches.value: קטיגורין: Greek κατήγορος via Aramaic, "accuser"; the -in ending is also the Aramaic plural, but the next words (הוא ירבעם) name one accuser. Translated, not transliterated
patches.reason: Proposed ruling: translate "accuser" in the English; the transliteration stays in this note
הגדלת (לעשות) echoes Joel 2:20 ("כי הגדיל לעשות"); "magnified" has no object

patches.value: הבאתם: second person plural, "you (and those with you) brought"; the address is singular elsewhere (ואתה, הזעקת). English cannot show the number
patches.reason: Number carried by a note

patches.value: את: the sign of the definite object; it has no English word
patches.reason: Learner note
לעפר בעפר is "to throw dust" (2 Sam 16:13, "ועפר בעפר"); "dust themselves" adds a reflexive
Follows 3:9.391
כמנהגי is plural
בספר מזויף is indefinite; "the forged book" adds the article

value: לא דייך שלא עשית (3:9.5-7): an idiom, "it was not enough for you that you did not do". The charge is not only the omission but the belief and acceptance that follow ("but", אלא).
בעד אחד ודיין אחד, ושלא בפני בעל דין, ובלא חקירה ובלא דרישה, ובלא בדיקה (3:9.16-29): the grounds of acceptance are listed in order, each negative with its own ובלא; the English keeps the repetition.

The Pesachim passage, after גרסינן, is Talmudic Hebrew with its own formulas (אמר רב ששת, כתיב בהדיא, וקרי ביה). It cites Exod 22:30 and Exod 23:1; the Talmud's reading (לא תשיא) is set against the written form (לא תשא).

The Machzor Vitry citation: the author introduces it (ובמחזור ויטרי ... על הא דתנן), quotes the Mishnah (אל תדון, printed על), and "כ' ע"ש" opens the quotation, which runs to עכ"ל. The opening formula stands outside the opening mark and the closing formula outside the closing mark. Inside it, single marks hold Solomon's wife's words, the voice, the bat kol and Hos 13:1. In ואתה מחייבו, "him" is Solomon.
הבאתם (3:9.371) is second person plural, while the address is singular elsewhere (ואתה, הזעקת, והוספת): "you (and those with you)".
The last part turns from the story to the addressee: ואתה הגדלת (and you have magnified) and כי אחרי אשר (for after) make the charge that his informing brought the author to prison.

value: Bat kol (literally "daughter of a voice"): a heavenly voice, the rabbinic way in which a voice from heaven speaks to a person. Here it speaks to Jeroboam son of Nebat in the story the author cites from Machzor Vitry.
Machzor Vitry: a compilation of prayers, laws and customs from the school of Rashi, attributed to Rabbi Simchah of Vitry, his pupil; it includes tractate Avot with a commentary.

Jeroboam son of Nebat: an Ephraimite, the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel after Solomon (1 Kgs 11-12). The tale of how he was tricked into oversleeping comes from rabbinic tradition, not from the Book of Kings.
The seven inquiries (שבע חקירות): the questions about time and place that a court puts to witnesses; the author names no source.
